transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I, uh… I came in because these flashes keep hitting me out of nowhere. Like I’ll be doing something totally normal, just standing at a pickup counter for work, waiting for someone to hand me a package, and suddenly it’s like I’m back in that crowded holding room. I can see the fight again, like it’s right there, and I hear everybody getting shoved up against the wall, all the noise and yelling and bodies moving around.

It doesn’t feel like just “remembering,” if that makes sense. It kind of takes over for a second, and I’m not really where I’m standing anymore. That’s the part that scared me enough to come in, because it keeps happening when I’m just trying to get through my day.
Can you tell me more about these flashes? Do they feel like you’re actually reliving the event, and how often do they occur?

Yeah… yeah, it does feel like I’m reliving it, not like I’m sitting there choosing to think about it. It’s more like it drops over me all at once. I’ll be at work, like at a pickup counter, just waiting for somebody to bring a package out, and then the room around me kind of… I don’t know, it’s like it gets replaced for a second.

I’m back in that crowded holding room. I can see people moving fast, the fight starting, and I can hear everybody yelling and bodies getting shoved up against the wall. It’s so clear that my body reacts before I even understand what’s happening. I’ll be standing there, but in my head it’s like I’m not there anymore.

It’s been happening out of nowhere, more than once, enough that I’m worried about going into places where I have to wait around with people close to me. I can’t really predict it. Sometimes nothing obvious sets it off except just being in a busy place or standing there waiting, and then suddenly I’m right back in it.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain places or situations because they remind you of that experience?

Yeah. I mean… yes, definitely. I didn’t even realize how much I was doing it at first, but I’ve been changing my routes and my work stuff around it.

Like, I’ve been turning down night runs, which I usually wouldn’t do, because some of those routes take me too close to that detention building. And even during the day, I’ll take this stupid long way around town just so I don’t have to pass anywhere near it. It adds time, it messes with my deliveries, but when I think about going by there my whole body just kind of locks up, like I can’t make myself do it.

And it’s not only the building. I don’t really talk about what happened if I can avoid it. If somebody asks too directly, I feel like I’m getting pulled right back into it again, like I’m not just explaining something that happened, I’m there. So I kind of shut it down or change the subject, or I just say I’m fine and move on, even though I’m obviously not acting fine.
